advances: An inclusion and volume gain for each fixed original cap. It does not compare the minimum-cap dispersion with the total residual gain.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
In the genuine two-contact situation the nonpositive margin at $(1,0)$ of a critical cap at $(0,0)$ gives $c_i\ge0$. In fact, a positive margin there would allow a small positive threshold increase keeping $(1,0)$ and deleting positive mass from a proper inball section at the left anchor, contradicting that both marks have global maximal depth. The stated normal form suffices for the proof even without criticality.

At $z(t)=-t/(1-t)$ the original cap inequality becomes $v_i\cdot x+c_i t\ge0$ after multiplying by $1-t$ and using scaled continuous coordinates. Therefore the displayed closed halfspace identifies the missed set up to a null boundary. Its transverse body $E_i^-$ contains zero and at least a half-ball in the relative interior ball of $E$ about zero; if the restriction of $v_i$ to $u^\perp$ vanishes the whole ball remains. Thus its $(d-1)$-volume is positive.

If $x\in U_i(t)$ and $e\in E_i^-$, the transverse inclusion of the slab theorem puts $x+(t-s)e$ in $D_s$. The same point satisfies $v_i\cdot(x+(t-s)e)\le-c_i t+(t-s)c_i=-c_i s$, proving the inclusion for the original cap. Since the transverse body is still in $u^\perp$, each individual slice inherits the inclusion. The slice integration, concave moment comparison and integer rescaling from the pair-residual theorem now apply with $D_t,D_s,E$ replaced by $U_i(t),U_i(s),E_i^-$. This gives both the all-dimensional bound and its stated integer planar form.
statement:
In the actual projective slab setting with $C_z,J,E,z(t),D_t$ as in the transverse-gain theorem, take an original left nonvertical cap $G_i=\{v_i\cdot x-c_i z\ge0\}$, where $v_i\ne0$ and $c_i\ge0$. For $0\le s<t<1$ with existing remote section put
$$
U_i(t)=D_t\cap\{v_i\cdot x\le-c_i t\},\qquad
E_i^-=E\cap\{v_i\cdot e\le c_i\}.
$$
Then $E_i^-$ has positive $(d-1)$-volume and
$U_i(t)+(t-s)E_i^-\subseteq U_i(s)$. The transverse gain for the pair residual applies to each $U_i$ with its own volume, width and body $E_i^-$. In the plane, for the unscaled area $U_{i,j}$ and width $w_{i,j}$ of the pair residual at $-j$ missed by the original $G_i$, using closed versions up to null boundaries, this gives
$$
(j+1)^2 U_{i,j-1}-j^2 U_{i,j}\ge j|E_i^-|_1 w_{i,j}.
$$
title: Transverse growth of each original left-cap missed residual
